Article Title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 10 lakh aid after Kulgam terror attack kills two labourers
Article Text:
The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where unidentified gunmen opened fire on the workers

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of two migrant labourers from Chhattisgarh who were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in Kulgam district.The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where unidentified gunmen opened fire on the workers. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work after leaving their villages in Chhattisgarh.One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital. The second victim, 28-year-old Bhupendra Bhaina, was initially admitted to Government Medical College, Anantnag, before being shifted to SKIMS Hospital in Srinagar, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Deepak, from Bundeli village in Sakti district, was the sole breadwinner for his family, which includes his elderly mother, a physically disabled younger brother, his wife and their four-month-old son. His uncle said Deepak had moved to Jammu and Kashmir around seven to eight months ago with his wife to work at the brick kiln in the hope of building a better future.Bhupendra, from Chhuiya village in Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district, had reached Kashmir around three months ago with his wife.The couple had left their four-year-old son in the care of his grandmother and younger sister while other family members worked as labourers in Himachal Pradesh.Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai expressed grief over the killings, describing the attack as "cowardly". He said the state government stood firmly with the bereaved families and had directed officials to coordinate with the Jammu and Kashmir administration to bring the bodies back home.
Article Summary: The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work. One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital.

Article Title: PM Modi inaugurates Rs 5,000 crore Bhogapuram Airport in Andhra Pradesh
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh 's Vizianagaram district, a nearly Rs 5,000 crore project that the state government says will transform North Andhra into a major economic and industrial hub.The PM was accorded a grand ceremonial welcome, with around 13,500 tribal women performing the traditional Dhimsa dance. The airport premises were adorned with displays celebrating Andhra Pradesh's rich cultural heritage, including Etikoppaka artwork and motifs depicting the state's geographical identity.PM Modi was received by Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu, deputy chief minister Pawan Kalyan, and union civil aviation minister K Ram Mohan Naidu. He later witnessed the Dhimsa performance before formally inaugurating the airport.Developed by the GMR Group, the airport has been named after freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju. It has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in its first phase, with a long-term expansion plan to increase capacity to 40 million passengers a year. Commercial flight operations are scheduled to begin on August 17.The Andhra Pradesh government has projected the airport as a key catalyst for industrial growth, employment generation, exports, skill development and improved connectivity across North Andhra.Following the inauguration, chief minister Naidu felicitated PM Modi with a traditional shawl before he laid the foundation stone, inaugurated and dedicated multiple development projects worth over Rs 17,900 crore. During the visit, Naidu and Union minister Ram Mohan Naidu also briefed the Prime Minister on the airport's features and future development plans.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh's Vizianagaram district. The airport is a nearly Rs 5,000 crore project that the state government says will transform North Andhra into a major economic and industrial hub.

Article Title: 'Forgiveness only on reel or will you withdraw cases?': Abhijeet Dipke comments on PM Modi's late night video
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's call for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest has triggered a fresh response, with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioning whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words.Reacting to the Prime Minister's selfie-style Instagram video, Dipke wrote, "Fraand, sirf reel par hi maaf karoge ya cases bhi wapas loge?(Friend, will you forgive them only through reels, or will you also withdraw the cases?)"The Prime Minister's video, shared on his official Instagram and X handles on Friday, came after a 15-year old protester from Noida was booked for allegedly using derogatory language against him during at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In the video, PM Modi said, "Today I just feel like talking to you. The country and the world have witnessed what happened at Jantar Mantar. Some mischievous children used very crude and abusive language, words that do not befit any civilized society. I was personally abused, and even my late mother was subjected to abuse. It was a truly ugly spectacle."Acknowledging the public outrage over the incident, the Prime Minister urged people to view the matter through the lens of reform rather than punishment.He said that while the students' remarks had understandably outraged society, mistakes are part of growing up. He urged people to forgive them, guide them in the right direction, and help them reform, saying the students had "lost their way" but deserved an opportunity to correct themselves.The Prime Minister further argued against prolonged legal action and social ostracisation."Punishing them, dragging them through court proceedings, and harassing them in society, none of this will change the situation. I want to forgive them. Society, too, should accept this," PM Modi said, while urging the students to learn from their mistakes and move forward.Earlier, Dipke had questioned the police action and alleged selective enforcement of the law.In a video shared by CJP on X, he said, "If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT Cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?"He further alleged that several social media users identifying themselves with the BJP had routinely targeted women online."They have been using all kinds of words, not respecting women from any angle. And they proudly wrote in their bio, 'Followed by PM Modi'. Such people have abused girls. When will the case be filed on them?" Dipke said.Questioning the criminal proceedings, Dipke argued that abusive language, while objectionable, should not automatically attract criminal prosecution."If cases are to be filed for abusing, highest number of cases will be filed against the BJP's IT Cell, because they are the ones who have abused women the most. And it will be against BJP's leaders, who have used bad language for years, even inside the Parliament," he said.In a post accompanying the video, CJP asked, "Will an FIR be filed against all those IT Cell members who have been abusing women for the last several years?"This is not the first time Dipke has publicly reacted to one of the Prime Minister's social media videos. Earlier on Thursday, after PM Modi released a video message highlighting the recently passed anti-paper leak legislation, Dipke commented on Instagram, "Your skin is brighter than the country's future."The Prime Minister had described the legislation as a key reform aimed at strengthening the examination system.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words. Dipke had questioned the police action and alleged selective enforcement of the law.

He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection," Ramesh said.Referring to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and student protests, Ramesh said, "the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors."He also said the Prime Minister owed an apology over the "Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka by the Ram Mandir Trust" and for the "Tughlakian notebandi of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs."Ramesh added, "but late last night, in act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth." Let’s guide the misguided. Let’s work together. Let’s work for Bharat," PM Modi wrote, sharing the video on X.In the video, PM Modi also highlighted the government's efforts to strengthen the country's examination system, citing Parliament's passage of a stringent anti-paper leak law."Friends, we are continuously taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. Article Title: FSSAI cracks down on three firms over food safety violations

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a fresh enforcement drive against food business operators, issuing a product recall, suspending a manufacturing licence and prohibiting the sale of a health supplement over serious violations of food safety regulations.In one action, FSSAI ordered M/s Sun Organic Industries Pvt Ltd to immediately recall its Wonderland Raisins after regulatory testing found pesticide residues exceeding the prescribed limits. Samples tested at both the National Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad, and the Referral Laboratory, NIFTEM-K, were declared "unsafe" under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The company has been directed to recall the entire batch from the market and submit periodic recall status reports.In a separate action, the food regulator suspended the licence of Dior Pharmaceuticals' Nutraceutical Manufacturing Unit with immediate effect after an inspection revealed major and critical non-compliances. According to FSSAI, the unit failed to comply with several regulatory and hygiene requirements, including inadequate quality management systems and deficiencies in manufacturing practices.FSSAI also issued a prohibition order against M/s Vatave Health Care, banning the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of its Folineuro Syrup (Folinic Acid Syrup). The regulator said the product was marketed as a nutritional food supplement with misleading claims related to brain function despite not complying with provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2016.The regulator said the actions were taken to protect consumers and ensure compliance with food safety laws. It warned that violations of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, would invite strict legal and penal action.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a fresh enforcement drive against food business operators. The regulator has issued a product recall, suspended a manufacturing licence and prohibited the sale of a health supplement over serious violations of food safety regulations.

Article Title: 'Same people who litter here, use dustbin abroad': Bombay HC on civic sense
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Friday came down heavily on Indians who litter public places at home but follow cleanliness rules abroad, saying the same people who "throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid" in India ensure to put "even a small chocolate wrapper" in the dustbin abroad.The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders.A bench of Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground in Mumbai.The judges said public participation was essential to keeping the city clean and urged civic authorities to enforce the rules without hesitation."If a person wants a clean environment, then he or she has a corresponding fundamental duty towards society to maintain cleanliness. We want the civic officials to be ruthless in taking action," the court said according to news agency PTI.Expressing concern over people's attitude towards public cleanliness, the bench said citizens often behave differently once they leave India."We have to sensitise our citizens. Here, a person will throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid, but these same people, when abroad, will strictly avoid such behaviour.Even a small chocolate wrapper they will throw in the dustbin," the high court said.The bench then questioned, "Is this the price of liberty and democracy?"The court also voiced concern over the large quantity of plastic waste strewn across public places, observing that even Mumbai's beaches are littered with plastic. It questioned whether such conditions reflected the standards of "a civilised society".The judges noted that garbage dumped on roads and in narrow lanes poses serious health and hygiene risks to residents every day.Referring to the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai's slogan 'Swachch Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai, Aapli Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai', the court said the civic body's intention was commendable but was being undermined by irresponsible behaviour from citizens and inadequate enforcement by the municipal machinery."It is in these circumstances the role of MCGM's cleanliness machinery wardwise becomes significant, to take all effective steps so that public streets are not used by the citizens as dumping places," the bench observed.The court said failing to enforce the rules would defeat the objective behind the civic body's cleanliness campaign and urged authorities to implement the existing regulations strictly.It also raised concerns over the handling of garbage near heritage landmarks such as Rajabai Tower and the Bombay high court building. The bench observed that tourists, including foreign visitors, often encounter garbage on roads because of poor waste handling by municipal collection vehicles.The high court directed the civic body to take corrective steps within a week, warning that it would otherwise be compelled to pass further orders.
Article Summary: The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders. Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground.

NEW DELHI: The death toll in Friday night's terror attack on migrant labourers in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam rose to two on Saturday after a Chhattisgarh worker succumbed to injuries in hospital, officials told news agency PTI.The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where the two workers were employed at a brick kiln. Officials said both men sustained critical injuries after terrorists fired at them.One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College (GMC) Anantnag before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Officials said both victims were in their twenties and had travelled from Chhattisgarh in search of work.The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi at Anantnag's Lal Chowk while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. That attack, on July 22, was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam massacre, in which 26 people were killed.Friday's attack has also revived concerns over the safety of migrant workers in the Valley. In February 2024, two non-local labourers from Punjab, Amritpal Singh and Rohit Masih, were shot dead in Srinagar. Before that, in October 2021, terrorists killed two workers from Bihar, Raja Reshi Dev and Joginder Reshi Dev, in Kulgam's Wanpoh area.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha condemned the latest attack and said security forces had been instructed to intensify anti-terror operations."I strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists," Sinha wrote on X, adding that he had spoken to DGP Nalin Prabhat and other senior security officials.PDP president and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti also condemned the killings."They work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence," she said.BJP's Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the attack as "cowardly, barbaric and inhuman", alleging that its objective was to disturb peace and normalcy in the Union Territory.The attack occurred during the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, which began on July 3. While the pilgrimage through the Pahalgam route has remained suspended since July 19 because of heavy rain and landslides, the Baltal route in Ganderbal continues to remain operational.Following the attack, security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in the area to trace those responsible.
Article Summary: The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura.

NEW DELHI: A 52-year-old BSF constable who recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of an Indian UN peacekeeping contingent has been admitted to the isolation ward at the Ebola Nursing Home of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital after developing fever during mandatory quarantine, triggering Ebola surveillance protocols.The constable, who arrived in India on July 11, had been under a 21-day quarantine at the Airport Health Organisation (APHO) facility following his return from Congo, an Ebola-endemic region. Suspected cases are isolated immediately and samples are tested at designated reference laboratories before a diagnosis is confirmed.

Article Title: Tahir Hussain gets life for IB staffer’s killing in 2020 riots
Article Text:
'

Only death sentence will be justice’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bringing the six-year-long trial in the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma to a close, a Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment, holding that Sharma was lynched “solely on account of his religion” during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.Additional sessions judge Parveen Kumar Singh, however, declined the prosecution’s plea for the death penalty, ruling that while the brutality of the crime was undeniable, the prosecution had failed to prove any specific act committed by each convict during the murder.Pronouncing the sentence, Singh described the murder as one of exceptional brutality committed during the “communal violence that erupted in the wake of the protests against CAA/NRC”.The court held that the prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had “aided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assembly”. Singh rejected the other convicts’ pleas that they were sole breadwinners. However, he did consider their educational background as a mitigating factor.On July 13, the court had convicted Hussain and four others, holding that the five were part of “a large crowd which, with animus against Hindus, had assembled...with a common object to commit rioting, loot, arson and to cause damage to the property and person of members of the Hindu community”, before murdering the IB staffer on Feb 25, 2020, whose body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was sentenced to six months’ RI under IPC Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148, seven years under Section 365 and imprisonment for life under Section 302. All sentences will run concurrently. He was also fined Rs 1,000 under Section 188, Rs 20,000 each under Sections 153A, 147 and 148, Rs 50,000 under Section 365 and Rs 5 lakh under Section 302, with default sentences in case of non-payment.“The manner in which it was committed was of the utmost brutality. The victim was sucked in by the murderous mob, baying for blood... The assault was so fierce, unrelenting, and from such close quarters that even in death, the body did not immediately slump to the ground,” the judge held.The court noted that the violence did not end with Sharma’s death. His body, it observed, was strapped “like an animal”, dragged to Chand Bagh pulia and thrown into a drain. Calling it an “aggravating circumstance of immense magnitude”, the judge remarked, “As if the hatred had still not been satiated, the dead body was thereafter thrown into the nala. Therefore, the barbarity with which this horrendous murder was committed is nauseatingly sickening. ”Saying the “crime test” tilted the case towards the “rarest of rare” category, the judge weighed aggravating and mitigating circumst-ances before declining the capital punishment sought by special public prosecutor Madhukar Pandey, who maintained that the offence was part of “well-orchestrated communal violence” rather than a crime committed und-er sudden provocation.The court zoomed in on what it found to be the prosecution’s principal shortcoming — the lack of specificity regarding the individual role of each convict. Observing that “before a life is ordered to be extinguished by a judicial decree”, something more than mere membership of an unlawful assembly had to be proved, the judge held that the prosecution had failed to bridge that gap. While acknowledging the state’s contention that the use of a heavy cutting weapon reflected pre-planned and cold-blooded intent, the court said the time for drawing such inferences was long past and treated the lack of specificity as a “huge mitigation. ”Judge Singh rejected the convicts’ pleas that they were sole breadwinners and noted that the “monstrosity of the crime committed outweighs this mitigating circumstance”. At the same time, he found no material to conclude that they were beyond reform.It also noted that allegations of Hussain’s house being used as a “launchpad” for the riots were neither part of the charges framed nor specifically proved during trial. The judge also took note of the “entirely satisfactory” custodial conduct of Hussain, Kasim and Nazim, barring minor infractions by Kasim.Another mitigating factor, the court said, was the educational background of the convicts. It observed that “vested interests” had spread misinformation and whipped up a “religious frenzy”, making the uneducated co-convicts “more gullible and susceptible to such propaganda”, and held that this vulnerability to manipulation was relevant while determining the sentence.Hussain’s co-convicts were awarded life imprisonment under Section 302 IPC with a fine of Rs 25,000 each. They were also sentenced to six months under Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148 and seven years under Section 365 IPC, along with fines ranging from Rs 1,000 to Rs 10,000 under the respective provisions. All the sentences will run concurrently.As Hussain was being led out of the courtroom by police after the sentencing, he turned to those present and said, “High court se insaaf milega. Der aaye, lekin durust aaye.”Speaking to TOI, Ankur Sharma, brother of the IB staffer, said, “From day one, this has been a ‘rarest of rare’ case. While we appreciate that the trial court has delivered a conviction and handed down life imprisonment, true justice won’t be served until the perpetrators receive the death sentence, a demand we will aggressively pursue in the high court. The sheer brutality of the crime still haunts our family every single day; knowing he was inflicted with 51 wounds, subjected to acid, and dumped in a drain is a pain that never truly goes away. ”
Article Summary: Former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others sentenced to life imprisonment. Sharma was lynched “solely on account of his religion’ during 2020 northeast Delhi riots. Prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had “aided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assembly.

Article Title: Amid opposition protest, Lok Sabha passes births & deaths bill

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without a debate and Rajya Sabha couldn’t transact any business Friday, amid sloganeering by opposition members over paper leaks, police crackdown of protesters and Ram temple “theft” issues.The bill was taken up for consideration and passage as soon as Lok Sabha reassembled after an hour-long adjournment at noon with BJP MP Dilip Saikia in the chair, leaving the opposition surprised as the house’s legislative business list showed it being listed against the name of home minister Amit Shah — who was not present — for moving it for passage.Several opposition members trooped into the well of the House, demanding Shah’s presence in LS, leading to the bill — seeking to amend provisions of the 1969 law to encourage timely registration of births and deaths — being passed by voice vote. Congress’s KC Venugopal and other MPs opposed its passage without debate.The bill proposed to make delayed registration of births and deaths stringent by requiring an order from a judicial magistrate (first class) for registrations after two years of the event.While Congress vehemently raised the issue of police crackdown on students, SP MPs were seen carrying placards of “chanda chor” to highlight the alleged temple donation theft.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said it was unfortunate the opposition did not participate in the discussion, despite agreeing in the business advisory committee meeting.As proceedings began in RS, several opposition MPs demanded LoP Mallikarjun Kharge be allowed to speak, but chairperson C P Radhakrishnan ticked them off, saying they were still in “Emergency mode” and that they must also listen to others. As opposition members continued to raise slogans, agriculture minister Shivraj Chouhan accused them of indulging in “sadak-chhap (cheap)” politics and said, “They’re doing petty politics, playing with the dignity of the House. Democracy is being destroyed...”. RS was adjourned for the day around 11:20 pm.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without a debate. Rajya Sabha couldn't transact any business Friday, amid sloganeering by opposition members over paper leaks, police crackdown of protesters and Ram temple "theft" issues.

Article Title: Monsoon likely to be ‘below normal’ in Aug-Sept: IMD
Article Text:
July rain gives hope to farm sector

NEW DELHI: Average rainfall in India during the second half of monsoon season (Aug-Sept) is most likely to be ‘below normal’, IMD said Friday, flagging the continuing risk of El Niño, which is associated with a weak monsoon.Last month, IMD had cited El Niño’s impact to forecast below normal rains in July. The month’s rainfall turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. The met department attributed this to “intra-seasonal variability”, saying a record 24 days were under the influence of ‘low pressure systems’ (LPS) in July against normal of about 13.5 days.“Four LPS were formed over Bay of Bengal that led to good rainfall from Odisha to Gujarat. We need to further analyse the reason (for better-than-expected July rains). These LPS couldn’t be captured by our long-range forecast model,” said Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD chief.Two long wet spells, one during the first week of July and the second from July 22 onwards, helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit in the country from 35% in June to nearly 13% at the end of July. Since the ‘monsoon core zone’, where farming operations remain mainly rain-fed, largely coincides with central India, good rains in the region could aid recovery of acreage in the month.Though overall acreage of the summer sown crops continues to be in deficit compared to the corresponding period last year, the deficit reduced from nearly 21% on July 3 to around 3% on July 31, giving hope to the farm sector in an El Nino year.During Aug-Sept, IMD said certain parts of peninsular India, central India, northern parts of northwest India, and east and northeast India may get “normal to above-normal” rains, but it may not change the forecast of overall ‘below normal’ quantitative rainfall in the country.
Article Summary: Average rainfall in India during the second half of monsoon season is most likely to be ‘below normal’ IMD flagging the continuing risk of El Niño, which is associated with a weak monsoon. Last month, IMD had cited El Niño’s impact to forecast below normal rains in July.

The 91-octane standard E20 petrol now costs Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi, while 100-octane petrol is priced at Rs 169 per litre.The ministry also rejected allegations that foodgrain meant for poor was being diverted for ethanol production or that subsidised FCI rice was being used to support the programme.
Article Summary: Petrol would have cost around Rs 125 a litre in the national capital when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel. 20% of every litre comprised domestically produced ethanol procured at pre-agreed prices. NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. NEW DELHI: Cabinet Friday approved two strategic tunnel projects and the approach roads on NH-244 in J&K at an estimated cost of around Rs 9,800 crore to provide all-weather connectivity between Kashmir Valley and Jammu region while improving access to Chenab Valley.The projects comprise Singhpora-Vailoo tunnel and Sudhmahadev-Dranga tunnel, along with their approach roads, on the Anantnag-Chenani corridor. These are expected to strengthen road connectivity in Doda, Kishtwar and Udhampur districts, and reduce travel time.While the 39-km Singhapora-Vailoo stretch will have 10-km unidirectional twin-tube tunnels, the 13-km Sudhmahadev–Dranga section will have 8-km twin tube tunnels. Once completed, the projects will provide a safer and more efficient route for commuters, tourists and freight movement.Officials said the projects would boost regional connectivity by ensuring year-round access to remote districts, facilitating faster movement of essential goods and emergency services. Improved road infrastructure is also expected to promote tourism, trade and economic activity in the Chenab Valley, besides creating employment opportunities during the construction phase.The tunnel projects form part of the Centre’s broader strategy to modernise transport infrastructure in J&K and improve connectivity to border and hilly regions. Govt has undertaken several major road projects in the Union Territory, including the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel, the Zojila Tunnel and the Z-Morh Tunnel, to provide seamless and all-weather road links.

NEW DELHI: Implementing its view that bail granted by a HC should not be ordinarily challenged in the apex court, Supreme Court Friday dismissed Uttarakhand's appeal questioning the grant of bail to one Abdul Malik , the alleged mastermind of a mob that hurled a petrol bomb to torch a police station in Haldwani in 2024.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked whether throwing a bomb constitutes an offence under UPA. "Is throwing a bomb a UAPA offence?" the bench asked the state additional advocate general Gaurav Bhatia before he could open arguments for cancellation of bail granted to Malik by HC."If a mob burns a police station, how is it an offence under UAPA? How did the offence affect national security? We have doubts about invocation of UAPA charges against the accused, that is why we are not inclined to entertain the appeal," Justice Bagchi said.Bhatia tried to impress upon the court the seriousness of the offence. "The accused is the mastermind behind mobilising the mob and one of his key associates threw petrol bombs to burn the police station, which is an offence that attracts a life sentence. Just because some co-accused got bail, he should not be granted the same relief without appreciating the gravity of the crime committed by him," he said.When the AAG said the HC passed a cursory order granting bail without giving reasons, the CJI said, "In light of the facts of the case, there was no need for a detailed order.SC has ruled repeatedly that bail should not be granted mechanically. Here the judge has applied his mind before granting bail."Bhatia said if a person who engineers such violence gets bail then it would have a demoralising effect on the police force. The bench disagreed and said, "If that is the concern of the state, then its prosecution should have ensured speedy trial and provided cogent evidence to secure conviction of the accused."The apex court bench dismissed the appeal but clarified that it has expressed no opinion on the merits of the case.
Article Summary: Supreme Court dismisses Uttarakhand's appeal questioning the grant of bail to one Abdul Malik. Malik is alleged mastermind of a mob that hurled a petrol bomb to torch a police station in Haldwani in 2024. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked whether throwing a bomb constitutes an offence under UPA.

NEW DELHI: India has screened 10,974 international travellers arriving from Ebola-affected countries since May 23 after the World Health Organization declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), with no case detected in the country so far, the Centre informed Parliament on Friday.The government said surveillance and preparedness were intensified across the country following the WHO declaration, with enhanced screening at airports and other points of entry, mandatory travel declarations, designated isolation facilities, expanded laboratory capacity and nationwide mock drills to prepare for any suspected case.According to the ministry of health and family welfare, all international passengers are screened for recent travel to Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and South Sudan—countries affected by the Ebola outbreak. The government has not imposed a blanket travel ban, but passengers with travel history to these countries during the previous 21 days are identified through Self Declaration Forms, including the Air Suvidha 2.0 portal.Mumbai accounted for the highest number of screened passengers at 7,568, followed by Delhi (1,833), Hyderabad (532), Chennai (210), Bengaluru (205) and Ahmedabad (200). At the state level, Gujarat recorded the highest number of screened passengers (2,905), followed by Maharashtra (2,228), Uttar Pradesh (785), Tamil Nadu (731), Telangana (624) and Kerala (554).Replying to a question in the Lok Sabha, Union Health Minister J P Nadda said the Centre had coordinated its response with the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Civil Aviation and other agencies to strengthen surveillance and preparedness.The preparedness measures include issuing standard operating procedures covering surveillance, quarantine, laboratory testing, infection prevention and clinical management; identifying and operationalising isolation facilities across states and Union Territories; expanding diagnostic capacity through ICMR-NIV Pune and additional Biosafety Level-3 laboratories; deploying additional doctors and paramedical staff at major international airports; and conducting mock drills in designated hospitals nationwide.The government has also strengthened public awareness through airport displays, in-flight announcements, social media campaigns and a 24×7 national helpline while activating the NCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre to coordinate the response.The health ministry said no Ebola case has been reported in India so far.
Article Summary: India has screened 10,974 international travellers arriving from Ebola-affected countries since May 23. The government has not imposed a blanket travel ban, but passengers with travel history to these countries during the previous 21 days are identified. Article Title: The price of mockery
Article Text: Thirukkural with the Times explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’. Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love and is considered one of the great works ever on ethics and morality. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres. Motivational speaker, author and diversity champion Bharathi Bhaskar explores the masterpiece. There is a kind of ignorance that is harmless. Then there is another kind that troubles me deeply. It ridicules what it has never cared to learn. History, scholarship, art, music, literature and sacrifice become material for cheap amusement. The ancient Greeks called such people the Philistines . Whatever the label, the damage they cause is real. A recent television programme left me with precisely this feeling. It was presented as a comedy. Four young adults sat chatting casually. One participant asked the others, "Do you know V O C? What did he pull?" One participant guessed he must have been a boatman and therefore pulled a boat. Another remarked, "I thought he pulled a saree, like how Duryodhana did." In the Mahabharata, it was Dushasana, not Duryodhana, who dragged Draupadi's saree. The studio laughed. But who was really being laughed at? Not V O Chidambaram Pillai. It was our own history. V O C, revered as Kappalottiya Tamilan , challenged the British shipping monopoly by founding the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906. When Indian merchants suffered under the colonial shipping monopoly, he dared to dream of Indian-owned ships to sail between Tuticorin and Colombo. He raised funds, purchased two ships and stood up to an empire. The British retaliated with brutal vengeance. Arrested on charges of sedition, he was sentenced to rigorous imprisonment. Inside the prison, this distinguished lawyer was yoked to an oil press, forced to perform labour meant for bullocks. Those agonising years earned him the title Sekkizhuththa Semmal . Poverty marked the rest of his life, but his sacrifice became a foundation for India's political and economic freedom. It was this extraordinary life that became a punchline. Ignorance is never a crime. Ridiculing greatness is. Psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger described this tendency in 1999. The Dunning-Kruger effect explains how people with very little knowledge often possess enormous confidence while failing to recognise genuine expertise. Perhaps that is why a classical musician, an accomplished dancer, a gifted artist, a poet, a scientist or a freedom fighter can become easy targets. Even in schools, children who excel in studies are sometimes mocked or bullied simply because they perform well. Such ridicule often grows from insecurity, resentment and the inability to appreciate another's excellence. Thiruvalluvar recognised this danger centuries ago. He devoted an entire chapter to Periyaarai Pizhaiyaamai . In Kural 896 , he says: Eriyaal Sudappadinum Uyvuundaam; Uyyaar Periyaarp Pizhaithozhu Vaar One may escape from flames, but none escape the consequences of insulting the great Valluvar 's wisdom does not stop with freedom fighters or celebrated personalities. It quietly crosses the threshold of our homes. How often do we see ageing parents or in-laws spoken to with impatience, mocked or dismissed as outdated? More painful still, how often do parents remain silent when their own children belittle grandparents? Respect for elders is not an old-fashioned custom. It is the moral foundation of every enduring culture. The day we begin laughing at those who carried us before we could walk, taught us before we could read and sacrificed before we could dream, we have diminished ourselves. A society that mocks its achievers, bullies its brightest children and humiliates its elders is not progressing. It has quietly vanquished its soul.
Article Summary: Bharathi Bhaskar explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text 'Thirukkural' Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each.

Article Title: Floating solar plants get Rs 5,000cr push
Article Text: Seeking to increase the Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) capacity to 5,000 mw from 700 mw, the Centre Friday cleared a Rs 5,070 crore scheme to push development of floating solar projects along with storage set-ups with a minimum capacity of 2 hours. These aim to utilise existing water reservoirs to set up solar plants, helping eliminating competition for land resources. National Institute of Solar Energy declared Maharashtra (16.3 gw) has the highest FSPV potential, which followed by Madhya Pradesh (14.9 gw), and Karnataka (13.7 gw). TNN
Article Summary: The Centre Friday cleared a Rs 5,070 crore scheme to push development of floating solar projects. These aim to utilise existing water reservoirs to set up solar plants. Maharashtra (16.3 gw) has the highest FSPV potential, followed by Madhya Pradesh (14.9 gw), and Karnataka (13.7 gw).

Article Title: Govt extends PM-Kisan yojana
Article Text: Govt Friday approved continuation of the farmers’ income support scheme, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-Kisan) Yojana, from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with a total financial outlay of Rs 3.1 lakh crore. Under the scheme, eligible landholding farmer families get financial assistance of Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each. Govt said, “...This has enhanced farmers’ productive capacity...”
Article Summary: Govt Friday approved continuation of the farmers’ income support scheme, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi. Under the scheme, eligible landholding farmer families get financial assistance of Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each.

Article Title: Samudra Manthan gets Cabinet nod
Article Text: Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan Friday, a Rs 84,084-crore national offshore exploration programme to step up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins to reduce dependence on imports, reports Atul Mathur. The scheme aims to increase exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas through large-scale seismic surveys, exploratory drilling and creation of common offshore infrastructure in the next five years.
Article Summary: The scheme aims to increase exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas through large-scale seismic surveys, exploratory drilling and creation of common offshore infrastructure in the next five years. Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan Friday, a Rs 84,084-crore national offshore exploration programme.

Article Title: Reaction teams to flag 'fake info' on E20 blending

NEW DELHI: Learning from the recent student protests led by CJP, govt has set up a team of officials from multiple ministries to counter online “misinformation” on E20 fuel through coordinated efforts by different stakeholders, including vehicle manufacturers, dealers, vehicle testing agencies, oil marketing companies and fuel pump dealers. Ministries concerned are also setting up Quick Response Teams (QRTs) to flag fake content.TOI has learnt that the team of officials from different ministries, including I&B, road transport, heavy industries and petroleum, is working together to deal with both proliferation of wrong information and also to put across the details that are backed by scientific and research-based reports. It’s focusing both on the young generation who are more active on different social media platforms and the targeted age groups who own vehicles as well.People aware of the development said this was one such rare occasion when there is a “coordinated and concerted effort” by different departments to put forward govt’s views backed by facts and scientific proof rather than individual departments fighting their own battle. They added, besides countering claims and allegations, testimonies of users and assurances of both vehicle manufacturers and oil marketing companies are also being put on social media platforms for online viewers.Officials added that govt has attached greatest importance to counter the ongoing campaign against ethanol blending and demand for going back to E0 (pure petrol) amid different organisations and political parties trying to garner support from people.While Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal is holding a townhall against E20 in the capital on Saturday, activist Tehseen Poonawalla has announced a silent march and hunger strike in Delhi.
Article Summary: Ministries concerned are also setting up Quick Response Teams (QRTs) to flag fake content. It’s focusing both on the young generation who are more active on different social media platforms and the targeted age groups who own vehicles as well.

Article Title: Senthil Balaji gets pre-arrest bail from SC in Tasmac corruption case
Article Text: NEW DELHI: SC Friday granted pre-arrest bail to DMK's V Senthil Balaji in a corruption case related to Tasmac saying the state no longer suffers "from his so-called malefic influence". The court asked Balaji to scrupulously cooperate with the probe, not tamper with evidence or attempt to influence any witness and directed him to surrender his passport with the investigating officer. Seeking TN's response to Balaji's plea for quashing of the FIR, it warned him: "We will cancel or modify our order if there is breach of the bail conditions."
Article Summary: SC Friday granted pre-arrest bail to DMK's V Senthil Balaji in a corruption case related to Tasmac. The court asked Balaji to scrupulously cooperate with the probe, not tamper with evidence or attempt to influence any witness.

Article Title: SC gives Rs 15L to kin of man killed by stray bull
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Setting a benchmark for compensation in cases of human death caused by stray cattle, particularly at a time when such incidents are on the rise across the country, SC, in a first-of-its-kind case, awarded Rs 15 lakh in compensation to the family of a man who died in 2007 when a bull attacked him in Punjab.Indicating that the state govt could not abdicate its responsibility towards people who get injured or die because of stray cattle, a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh directed all states to frame rules "to develop a mechanism for payment of compensation in accidents caused as a result of bovine/cattle, in both categories of cases, i.e. pedestrian or vehicular". It also asked govt to take care of strays and take action against owners who leave their animals on the streets and highways.
Article Summary: First-of-its-kind case awarded Rs 15 lakh in compensation to the family of a man who died in 2007 when a bull attacked him in Punjab. Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh directed all states to frame rules "to develop a mechanism for payment of compensation"

Article Title: SC slaps Rs 1 lakh fine on Rajasthan government for harassing official
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Frowning upon "interference" by the joint secretary of the then chief minister of Rajasthan in May 2018 in a matter of granting sanction to prosecute a govt official, Supreme Court has directed the state to pay 1 lakh to the official for harassing him.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the provision of sanction was meant to safeguard innocent public servants from frivolous harassment."The decision-making process under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, cannot resemble the dilemma in Hamlet's Soliloquy: 'to be or not to be', though expressed in a different context. If there is ambivalence, it could be presumed that extraneous considerations weighed and here is a case where political dictate is blatantly displayed," the bench said.The bench took a serious view of the blatant display of "political dictate" by the state in dragging a public servant to court."We cannot but observe that the petitioner has been dragged unnecessarily to the high court by the review, prompted by the office of the CM. The state at least should have rested content, when the highest constitutional court within its boundaries interfered with a patently illegal and blatantly tainted order of sanction.We hence dismiss the special leave petition with the above observations and further direction to the state to pay cost quantified at 50,000 each before high court and this court," the bench said."The deliberate digression from essential duties, presumably on political considerations, commenced when the joint secretary of the chief minister on 24.05.2018 referred back the matter for reconsideration, asserting that the money recovered from the table drawer of the petitioner clearly proved the acceptance of bribe," it said.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the provision of sanction was meant to safeguard innocent public servants from frivolous harassment. The bench took a serious view of the blatant display of "political dictate" by the state in dragging a public servant to court.

Article Title: PM Modi, Burnham discuss trade pact in 1st call
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Congratulating UK PM Andy Burnham on assuming office, PM Narendra Modi said the two leaders will collaborate closely to fully harness the trade and investment opportunities presented by the recently operationalised India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), for the "shared prosperity and well-being of both our people".Burnham officially took office as UK PM on July 20, 2026.The leaders discussed the West Asia conflict, agreeing to continue to work closely together towards de-escalation and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. According to the UK, Burnham set out his ambitions to further enhance ties, including through the UK-India Vision 2035 framework.

Article Title: Cabinet eases captive waterfront norms to spur private investment
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Cabinet Friday approved a revision to the shipping ministry’s captive waterfront policy to accelerate private investment by providing greater operational certainty and allowing govt entities to obtain waterfronts on a nomination basis.The revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port-Dependent Industries (Captive Policy) introduces a series of reforms aimed at improving operational flexibility and strengthening infrastructure development at major ports.The shipping ministry said the revised policy allows existing captive users to develop additional berths, jetties, terminals and Single Buoy Moorings (SBMs) to meet enhanced captive requirements. It also extends the concession period to up to 30 years for govt entities while addressing changes arising from evolving business needs and regulatory conditions.Officials said there were around 24 captive waterfront facilities as of last year.“The policy is expected to provide greater certainty to investors, facilitate capacity augmentation and improve the ease of doing business in the port sector without any financial implication for the government,” the ministry said.The revised policy also provides a framework for allotting waterfronts and associated land to eligible government organisations on a nomination basis, without resorting to competitive bidding, subject to availability and prescribed safeguards.Eligible entities include Central and state govt departments, statutory authorities, autonomous bodies, public sector undertakings (PSUs) and government-controlled joint ventures operating in sectors such as fertilisers, food, petroleum, oil and gas, coal, and steel, as notified by the shipping ministry.Under the revised policy, concessions will be awarded at the notified floor price.
Article Summary: Cabinet Friday approved a revision to the shipping ministry’s captive waterfront policy. Reforms aimed at improving operational flexibility and strengthening infrastructure development at major ports. It also extends the concession period to up to 30 years for govt entities.

Article Title: J&K: Properties of 11 Pak-based terrorist handlers attached in Ramban
Article Text:

JAMMU: J&K Police attached properties of 11 Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Ramban district on Friday to prevent their misuse for terror financing in the Union Territory.The assets belonged to terrorist handlers Mohammed Iqbal, Farooq Ahmed, Bashir Ahmed, Atta Mohd Khanday, Mohd Yaseen, Tariq Hussain, Mohd Rafiq, Muzzafer, Abdul Qadir Naik, Mohd Iqbal Wani, and Abdul Waheed. A total of 15 kanals and three marlas of land, valued at approximately Rs 90.7 lakh, was attached. One kanal is approximately 5445sqft, while one marla measures around 272.2sqft.The attachment — linked to a case registered at Banihal PS under provisions of IPC and Unlawful Activities Prevention Act — was carried out by police teams from Banihal sub-division in the presence of executive magistrates and local witnesses, a police spokesperson said.“During investigation, credible evidence established that the accused had exfiltrated to Pakistan to attain terrorist training. They were currently operating as terrorist handlers from across the border, actively promoting, facilitating, and coordinating activities of ultras. The accused had allegedly planned to use the assets to facilitate, finance, and sustain terror acts,” the spokesperson said.The action was part of J&K Police’s ongoing efforts to dismantle the financial and logistical infrastructure of cross-border terror networks. In a similar exercise Thursday (July 30), police attached properties of five Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Reasi district. In yet another such operation on Wednesday (July 29), cops attached assets worth over Rs 90 lakh in Ramban district, belonging to four terrorist handlers operating from Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

NEW DELHI: The family of two convicts sentenced to life imprisonment in the Ankit Sharma murder case, along with former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain, on Friday said they would challenge the trial court's verdict in the Delhi High Court.Speaking to ANI, Mohammad Asif, the brother of convicts Nazim and Kasim, claimed that his brothers had been falsely implicated in the case and denied any connection with Tahir Hussain."We will appeal in the High Court. An example should be set so that such an incident never happens to anyone else," he added.The court has awarded life imprisonment to all five convicts. The prosecution had argued that Sharma suffered 51 injuries and was brutally assaulted before his body was dumped into a drain.

Article Title: 'Muslims can't regard country as deity': Islamic body objects to Vande Mataram Bill
Article Text:
The Board’s spokesperson, Dr SQR Ilyas, said that making Vande Mataram legally mandatory for all communities was incompatible with both constitutional principles and Islamic belief.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) on Friday strongly criticised Parliament’s passage of a Bill that makes alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence, calling it an attack on religious and constitutional freedoms and urging the government not to impose patriotic expressions through legal compulsion.In a press release issued on 31 July, the Muslim body said the legislation was contrary to the constitutional, secular and democratic ethos of the country and amounted to a serious assault on the religious freedom of citizens. It argued that compelling participation in a song or slogan carrying religious connotations violated fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.The Board’s spokesperson, Dr SQR Ilyas, said that making Vande Mataram legally mandatory for all communities was incompatible with both constitutional principles and Islamic belief.“Any attempt to make Vande Mataram compulsory for all sections and religious communities through legal coercion is not only objectionable but also contrary to the fundamental principles of the Constitution,” he said.The AIMPLB said that during the framing of the Constitution, the Constituent Assembly accepted only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram at the national level, while the religious connotations of the remaining portions were not considered compatible with India’s secular character.Dr Ilyas argued that certain passages of the song depict the motherland in the form of a goddess and exhort people to worship her, which he said was contrary to the Islamic doctrine of Tawheed, or the absolute Oneness of God.“Therefore, compelling a Muslim to participate in a song, slogan or practice carrying a religious meaning contrary to his or her faith is wholly unacceptable,” he said.The Board also cited Articles 25 and 19 of the Constitution, saying they protect the freedom of religion and freedom of expression, including the right not to participate in expressions that conflict with an individual’s conscience.“These constitutional safeguards clearly imply that no citizen can be compelled to adopt or participate in any song, slogan, ideology or symbol against his or her religious beliefs and conscience,” the statement said.Referring to the Supreme Court’s landmark judgment in Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala, Dr Ilyas said the court had upheld this principle even in the context of the national anthem.“The Court held that a person could not be punished merely for not participating in an act when doing so was contrary to his or her religious beliefs. The Court also made it clear that, in certain circumstances, freedom of expression includes the right to remain silent, and that respectful non-participation cannot be regarded as disrespect.”The AIMPLB sought to distinguish between patriotism and religious devotion, saying that love for one’s country should not be equated with worship.“Love for the motherland and worship of the motherland are two entirely different concepts. Muslims deeply love their country and consider love for the homeland part of their civic and moral responsibility, but they cannot regard the country as a deity or goddess.”The Board added that patriotism should be judged by a citizen’s commitment to the Constitution, the country’s people and their rights rather than by the recitation of a particular slogan or song.It also urged the government to prioritise issues such as unemployment, inflation, poverty, education, healthcare, economic inequality and social injustice instead of pursuing what it described as sensitive and divisive measures.“Diverting public attention from fundamental issues by inflaming emotional and religious controversies serves neither the national interest nor the cause of democracy.”Concluding its statement, the AIMPLB said that India’s unity could only be strengthened by protecting constitutional supremacy, religious freedom and equal rights for all citizens.“A strong and united India can only be built where every citizen enjoys equal dignity, justice and freedom; where anyone’s patriotism is not judged through the prism of his or her religious beliefs; and where the supremacy of the Constitution, religious freedom and fundamental civil rights are protected at all costs.”The Vande Matram Bill, passed by both Houses of Parliament on Friday, seeks to make alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence and gives legal backing to its mandatory observance in specified contexts. Supporters have described the measure as a way to promote national unity and respect for a national symbol, while critics argue that it could compel citizens to participate in patriotic expressions regardless of their religious beliefs or freedom of conscience, raising concerns over constitutional rights and religious freedom.
Article Summary: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) has strongly criticised Parliament’s passage of a Bill that makes alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence. The Board said the legislation was contrary to the constitutional, secular and democratic ethos of the country. It argued that compelling participation in a song or slogan carrying religious connotations violated fundamental rights.

Article Title: 'India always supportive of dialogue and diplomacy': Jaishankar speaks to Iran FM Araghchi
Article Text:
The conversation came as tensions between Iran and the United States intensified, with Tehran claiming fresh strikes on American military facilities in Kuwait (File photo)

NEW DELHI: India on Friday expressed deep concern over the escalating conflict in West Asia, with external affairs minister S Jaishankar speaking to his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi and urging restraint amid growing regional tensions.In a post on X after the conversation, Jaishankar said he had a "tele-conversation" with Araghchi and reiterated India's concerns over the deteriorating security situation. "Conveyed our deep concerns at the ongoing hostilities in the region," he wrote.Jaishankar also stressed the need to protect commercial shipping and seafarers as the conflict increasingly threatens key maritime routes. "Strongly urged that attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers be avoided under any circumstance. India condemns any such attack by any party," he said.The external affairs minister added that he was briefed on Tehran's position during the call. "Was apprised of Iran’s perspective of current developments and discussions underway. India is always supportive of dialogue and diplomacy," Jaishankar wrote.The conversation came as tensions between Iran and the United States intensified, with Tehran claiming fresh strikes on American military facilities in Kuwait.According to Iranian state media, the Iranian army carried out drone attacks on the US-operated Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base as part of the 27th phase of Operation Lightning. Tehran said the operation was launched in response to a recent US strike on a residential home on Qeshm Island, alleging that it targeted military infrastructure including aircraft shelters, satellite communication systems and equipment warehouses.Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) separately claimed responsibility for strikes on the US-operated Ali Al Salem airbase in Kuwait, saying it had destroyed drone hangars and a fuel storage facility. The IRGC also vowed to continue military operations until US forces leave the region.The United States, however, rejected Iran's claims. US Central Command (CENTCOM) said no American aircraft had been damaged in the attacks and that all missiles and drones had either been intercepted or failed to reach their intended targets.
Article Summary: India expresses deep concern over the escalating conflict in West Asia. External affairs minister S Jaishankar spoke to his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi. He urged restraint amid growing regional tensions. The conversation came as tensions between Iran and the United States intensified.
